clue.text: Dispirited after a pillow fight?

parts.note: a burst pillow leaves feathers everywhere, including in a fighter's open mouth, and the same phrase is an idiom for gloomy

explanation.surface: Someone feels low after a pillow fight ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase describes feathers (down) stuck in the mouth after a pillow fight; as an idiom it means glum.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a sad, downcast expression, so it means dejected.

clue.text: Corrupt society girl takes gold to church

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young woman entering high society
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A debutante brings gold to church and leads others astray.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprave or lead into vice is a verb sense of corrupt.

clue.text: Having an unusual feature -or a quarrel

explanation.surface: Something is distinctive, or else there is a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing done this way has a special twist; read literally, being with a difference of opinion is having a dispute.

clue.text: Very good turn by doctor on foot

indicators.note: turn tells us to flip the letters for very good so they run the other way

parts.note: AI (A1) means first-class, very good
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor does a very good turn on someone's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' looks medical beside 'doctor', but it is the metrical unit.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry a foot is a metrical unit, and this one is a short syllable followed by a long one.

clue.text: Is neat rum a medicinal concoction?

indicators.note: rum in its sense of odd or strange signals that the letters of is neat are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Is a neat measure of rum a cure for something?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink; it is the adjective meaning odd, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal infusion is drunk for its healing properties, a medicinal brew.

clue.text: Interpretation was and is about examples included

indicators.note: included shows the examples are set inside the pair made from was and is

parts.note: EX- as a prefix means former, what was
taken as written
EG is the abbreviation for example, so examples are written EGES

explanation.surface: A reading of a text was and still is about examples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' serves only as a link here. 'was' is the prefix ex- (former), and examples are e.g.'s, which the word 'included' sets between the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A critical explanation of a text, especially scripture, is its interpretation.

clue.text: Request a set of questions for use in parliament

parts.note: to order something is to request it
an exam paper is a set of questions

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a set of questions to be put in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the item is the daily agenda printed for use in the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily agenda listing the business of the House of Commons is printed for members in parliament.

clue.text: Go to beneficial feature and benefit from it

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
taken as written
an advantage is a beneficial feature

explanation.surface: Head for a good feature and profit from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to exploit a situation so as to profit by it.

clue.text: Sell door-to door, use a bike, say

indicators.note: say indicates the word for using a bike is spoken, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: to pedal is to work a bike's cranks with the feet

explanation.surface: A salesman goes house to house, perhaps on a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawker travels about offering goods, selling from house to house.

clue.text: Gamble with half coming back early

parts.note: a bet is a gamble

indicators.note: coming back tells us the word for half is read from its end to its start

parts.note: semi- is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: Someone places a bet and gets half the stake returned.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning in good time or soon, so early.

clue.text: Support witch's place to the south-east

parts.note: in the Bible the Witch of Endor summoned the spirit of Samuel for King Saul
SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: Someone backs a witch's home lying to the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: To back or approve a person or plan is a sense of support.

clue.text: Revolting like the tree

parts.note: a people up in arms are in revolt, so up means revolting
as means like, in comparisons

explanation.surface: Something disgusting resembles the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' reads as disgusting; it means rising in revolt, UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A Javanese tree with poisonous sap, famed in legend for killing nearby life.

clue.text: Turned red, a peculiarity that was not fully appreciated

indicators.note: peculiarity suggests oddness, signalling that the letters of turned red a are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone blushed at an oddity no one valued properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'peculiarity' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something valued below its worth is undervalued, its merits not fully recognised.

clue.text: Payment into sinking fund?

parts.note: a payment that clears a debt is one sense, and the subsidence of a building as it sinks is another

explanation.surface: Money is paid into a fund set aside to clear debts.
explanation.walkthrough: A sinking fund is money set aside to repay a debt; the word also means the gradual sinking of ground or a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying off an account is one meaning; a building's gradual subsidence is another.

clue.text: Hardly rained?

parts.note: read as rained hard-ly, it describes precipitation coming down as hard ice pellets

explanation.surface: There was barely any rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly' seems to mean barely; read as 'in a hard way', it describes frozen pellets falling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice pellets falling from clouds is rain in hard form.

clue.text: Give a car new home

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of give a car are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Hand over a car and a new house.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish clergyman's house is his home.

clue.text: Upend one contraption that was still sealed

indicators.note: a contraption is something cobbled together, so the letters of upend one are reassembled

explanation.surface: Tip over a gadget that has never been opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never yet broached remains closed, still sealed.

clue.text: Infer gut trouble when making a denial

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the letters of infer gut are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Concluding a stomach upset is the cause while denying it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut or disprove a claim is to deny it.

clue.text: Remember second ring?

explanation.surface: Recall a second phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as RE (again) plus CALL (ring), a repeat phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring to mind is to remember; a call made again is a second telephone ring.

clue.text: Hard worker in the building industry

definitions.text: Hard worker in the building industry

parts.words: Hard worker in the building industry
parts.note: an animal famed for industriousness builds dams, so it is a hard worker in building

explanation.surface: A diligent construction worker is praised.
explanation.walkthrough: The builder here is the dam-building rodent, also slang for a diligent worker.
explanation.definitionFit: The dam-building rodent is proverbially industrious, a busy worker.

clue.text: Trusting dependent

explanation.surface: Someone who trusts is dependent.
explanation.definitionFit: One who relies on another trusts them and is dependent on them.

clue.text: One in France is performing in harmony

parts.note: un is French for one
taken as written
a performer is on, on stage

explanation.surface: One person in France is singing in tune with others.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing or acting together as one is agreement, harmony.

clue.text: Agree to write

explanation.surface: Agree to send letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that match coincide or agree; exchanging letters is writing to each other.

clue.text: An illicit plant started producing dye

indicators.note: started means the answer is the start of the run an illicit

explanation.surface: An illegal crop has begun to yield colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ANIL starts the words 'An illicit'; 'plant' adds colour, as the same word names the indigo shrub the dye comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo, the blue colouring extracted from a shrub, goes by this name.

clue.text: The right colour?

parts.note: the political right in Britain, the Conservatives, use this colour as their own

explanation.surface: Is this the correct shade?
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' seems to mean correct; it is the political right, whose British party colour this is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Conservative party, on the political right, is identified with this colour.

clue.text: Case for travelling light

parts.note: a portable glass casing holds a flame, so it is a case for light carried about

explanation.surface: A suitcase suited to someone who packs little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling light' suggests packing little; it means a light that is carried around.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable lamp is a protective casing for a flame that can be carried.

clue.text: Fruit last month in hospital appeared initially

indicators.note: in shows the abbreviation for last month goes inside the word for hospital

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a hospital
ult. (ultimo) is the formal abbreviation for last month

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of appeared

explanation.surface: Fruit turned up in hospital last month.
explanation.definitionFit: A seedless dried grape is a fruit.

clue.text: Its events deter arrangement of financial stake

indicators.note: arrangement of tells us the letters of its events deter are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Happenings discourage a monetary interest in a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal interest, usually monetary, in a matter is a financial stake.
